description: Figure 1, titled "Number of tasks by language family," is a bar chart that displays the distribution of tasks across different language families. The horizontal axis lists the language families, which are presented in a specific order. The vertical axis represents the number of tasks, with a scale ranging from 0 to 300 in increments of 50. The chart shows that the Indo-European language family has the highest number of tasks, with a bar reaching a value of approximately 280. The Sino-Tibetan language family follows with a value of around 100 tasks. The remaining language families—Afro-Asiatic, Austronesian, Niger-Congo, and others—each have a significantly smaller number of tasks, with their bars indicating values of approximately 30, 20, 10, and 5 respectively. The chart clearly illustrates a large disparity in the number of tasks assigned to the Indo-European family compared to all other families.
